title: Advanced Missions & Optimization
contentStatus: Built per Content Principles (60% pass, terminology + notes). Final module of L2 - completes L1-L2 pilot cohort curriculum.

sections.title: Beyond Basic Missions
learningObjectives: Understand how mission complexity can extend beyond simple point-to-point tasks
Recognize this module's place as the capstone of L2
sections.content: Everything in L2 so far has built toward operating MoRo reliably day-to-day. This final L2 module looks at more complex mission patterns and introduces thinking about performance - not just whether a mission completes, but how efficiently. This is the bridge between operating MoRo and starting to optimize how it's used.

keyTerms.note: MoRo's Human-Machine Interface (HMI) platform, used for fleet monitoring, mission control, and programming.

sections.title: Complex Mission Patterns
learningObjectives: Understand the concept of missions with conditional logic
Recognize how loops and branches differ from simple linear missions
sections.content: Beyond simple point-to-point tasks, missions can include conditional logic (if a condition is met, take one path; otherwise, another) and repeating patterns (a loop that continues until a defined end state). These patterns let a single mission definition handle situations that would otherwise require many separate simple missions. Exact configuration of conditional logic within ANT will be confirmed against the live system.

keyTerms.note: Mission logic where the next action depends on whether a specified condition is met.

sections.title: Thinking About Performance
learningObjectives: Understand basic performance metrics relevant to mission execution
Recognize why performance awareness matters at the operator level
sections.content: Performance in this context means cycle time (how long a mission takes) and throughput (how much gets moved over a given period). You're not expected to optimize these yourself at L2, but recognizing that a mission is taking noticeably longer than usual - even if it still completes successfully - is useful information worth mentioning, since it can signal something worth investigating.

keyTerms.note: The time it takes for a mission to complete from start to finish.
The total amount of material or work moved over a given period.

sections.title: Route and Speed Considerations
learningObjectives: Understand at a conceptual level how routing choices affect efficiency
Recognize this as an area that deepens significantly at L3B
sections.content: Route planning and speed tuning affect how efficiently a fleet operates, but detailed optimization of these is L3B (Programmer) territory. At L2, the relevant awareness is simply that routes and speeds aren't arbitrary - they're chosen deliberately, and a route that looks inefficient to you may reflect constraints (safety zones, other unit traffic) not immediately visible.

sections.title: Data Logging
learningObjectives: Understand that MoRo records operational data automatically
Recognize the general purpose of this data
sections.content: MoRo logs data during operation - mission timing, completion status, and related metrics - automatically, without requiring operator action. This data supports the kind of performance analysis and troubleshooting covered at higher levels. At L2, you don't need to access or interpret this data directly; just be aware that it exists and that unusual events are generally captured.

sections.title: Completing L1-L2
learningObjectives: Recognize the full scope of what L1-L2 has covered
Understand the path forward into specialist tracks
sections.content: This module closes the L1-L2 curriculum. Together, these eleven modules have covered coexistence, interface operation, mission handling, payload coordination, battery management, fleet awareness, troubleshooting fundamentals, and now optimization awareness. From here, the curriculum branches into specialist tracks - L3A for technicians, L3B for programmers - each building on this operational foundation toward deeper, role-specific expertise.

questions.question: What does conditional logic in a mission allow for?
options: Different actions depending on whether a specified condition is met
questions.feedback: Correct. Conditional logic lets a mission branch based on conditions, rather than following one fixed path.

questions.question: What does 'cycle time' refer to?
options: The number of units in a fleet
The time for a mission to complete from start to finish
questions.feedback: Correct. Cycle time measures mission duration, start to finish.

questions.question: At L2, are you expected to actively optimize routes and speeds yourself?
options: No - that level of optimization belongs to L3B; L2 requires awareness only
Yes, this is a core L2 responsibility
questions.feedback: Correct. Detailed route and speed optimization is L3B (Programmer) territory.

questions.question: Does MoRo require operator action to log operational data?
options: Yes, data must be manually recorded
No - it logs data automatically during operation
questions.feedback: Correct. MoRo logs mission timing and status automatically, without operator input.

questions.question: What comes after completing L1-L2 in the curriculum?
options: Automatic certification with no further levels
It branches into specialist tracks: L3A for technicians, L3B for programmers
questions.feedback: Correct. L1-L2 is the operational foundation before branching into role-specific specialist tracks.
